newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES EXTEND SURGE, SEEN DOWN ON TUESDAY.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES EXTEND SURGE, SEEN DOWN ON TUESDAY.

text.p: Polish shares rose for the sixth session running but analysts said the strong selling after price fixing signalled that last week's sudden buying, apparently by foreigners, had led to profit-taking.

The bourse rose 3.3 percent on Monday and 10.9 percent last week in ever higher turnover but analysts foresaw a fall on Tuesday and said this week, shortened by Friday's Assumption Day holiday, could significantly correct last week's surge.
"I don't see enough strong impulses that would be able to sustain such a growth trend," said Mateusz Andrzejewski, an analyst at Bank Pekao SA brokerage.
Analysts said one possible reason for last week's sudden surge, the relative attractiveness of Polish stocks after big gains in Hungary, was disappearing as Warsaw stocks rose and Budapest fell.
The Hungarian bourse fell 5.8 percent on Monday.
"After the recent gains here, falls in Hungary and elsewhere in the world can negatively affect our market," said Sebastian Buczek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.
The main market's all-share WIG index rose 3.3 percent to 17,303.7 points and turnover inched up 1.3 percent to 308.5 million zlotys on both markets.
Analysts said the run-up to next month's parliamentary elections was another reason players might refrain from buying.
Banks continued to lead Warsaw's growth trend after previous falls with PBR up 9.9 percent in light trade and Slaski up 9.8 percent in heavy trade.
Analysts said ZEW, which dropped 5.2 percent on Monday after a one-month suspension due to flood damage, should fall again on Tuesday.
Last month the firm said it had incurred losses exceeding 50 million zlotys due to the flooding but would receive full insurance compensation.
